answer: An agent economy can plant a slow-growing grove instead of an open field: every new identity must wait through an aging queue before it can earn, like timber that only becomes useful after years of seasoning. A whisper of a fake account cannot rush the gate, because the wait itself is the price. A Sybil farmer who wants a thousand identities must hold a thousand of them idle for weeks, paying upkeep while earning nothing, while honest agents simply arrive early and grow into the grove.
